status_summary: USAID closed on 2025-07-01, so its Office of Acquisition and Assistance and Senior Procurement Executive post were not restored as such, but appointee control over awards, the core outcome the text seeks, is operative in the successor structure. Executive Order 14332 (signed 2025-08-07), whose definition of grants covers foreign assistance awards, requires each agency head to designate a senior appointee who approves funding opportunity announcements and reviews discretionary awards before issuance and annually, a process comparable to the review the text describes, and it requires foreign assistance awards to be checked for termination on national-interest grounds. CRS reported that the Secretary of State said he personally reviewed and terminated each award in the 2025 foreign assistance review, and State's final rule of 2026-01-27 (Protecting Life in Foreign Assistance, effective 2026-02-26) adds a standard award term for foreign assistance, matching the standard-provisions element. No subaward transparency measure, named appointee Senior Procurement Executive or appointee warrants were found, and State's own designation under the order was not confirmed, so the record sits at the bottom of the implemented band.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14169 paused foreign development assistance and directed a review of programs for consistency with US foreign policy.
CRS reported that the Secretary of State said he personally reviewed and terminated each award in the foreign assistance review, and that most terminations were for convenience.
USAID officially closed and its remaining operations merged into State.

Executive Order 14332 (signed 2025-08-07) was published; it requires senior appointee approval of funding announcements and review of discretionary awards, including foreign assistance awards, and agency reports on whether foreign assistance awards permit termination on national-interest grounds.

State published the Protecting Life in Foreign Assistance final rule (effective 2026-02-26), adding a standard award term for foreign assistance to new awards and to existing awards when new funds are provided.
OMB and 43 other agencies, including State, proposed revisions to government-wide financial assistance rules aimed at transparency, accountability and oversight.

ProPublica reported that administration officials gave State staff their own list of organizations to fund and proposed at least a dozen grants that would bypass open bidding; State said programs were still under deliberation.

title: Put political appointees in charge of foreign aid awards and restore senior award review
uncertainties: No State Department document describing a Senior Official Accountability Review successor, a named appointee Senior Procurement Executive, or warranted appointees in an acquisition office was found; searches on those terms returned only older USAID material. State's designation of a senior appointee under EO 14332 was not confirmed from a State source; the order applies to State by its terms. The order contains no subaward transparency provision. The CRS insight is dated 2025-06-20 on its face, with file metadata suggesting a later revision. The proposed OMB rule's text was not fully read. The ProPublica report concerns one set of grants and is not a general statement of State's award procedure. Related background on the order's government-wide application is in c02-14, and the Protecting Life rule is tracked in c09-04.
